inputs.share_count_basis: 88,241k shares outstanding net of 808,541 treasury shares at 2026-06-30 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin); FY2026 yuho states no potentially dilutive shares exist, so basic = fully diluted. Held flat: SBC-zero market, buybacks are de minimis (JPY1m FY2026).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 consolidated cash-flow statement (3101.T_Annual_FY2026.txt:720-760) carries no share-based payment add-back and the yuho discloses no stock-option or restricted-share plan; J-GAAP SBC-zero market. SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q1 FY2027 balance sheet (2026-06-30): cash and deposits 29,783 less total borrowings 255,819 (short-term borrowings + commercial paper + current bonds + current LT borrowings + bonds + LT borrowings, including the JPY40bn subordinated loan/bond raised Sept 2024). Finance-lease liabilities (6,535 at 2026-03-31) are NOT in total_debt and are deducted separately in equity_bridge. FY2026 year-end comparables: cash 31,107 / debt 254,471 / net debt 223,364.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built unlevered cost of capital, not a levered WACC: 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct 2026) + asset beta ~0.7 x JPY ERP 6.0% = 5.9%, rounded to 6.0%. A mechanical levered WACC would be ~4-4.5% (market E/V ~37%, pre-tax Kd 1.15% = 2,920 interest on ~255bn debt) because 63% of the capital is near-zero-cost yen debt; discounting unlevered flows at that rate would capitalise the tax shield of a 4.4x ND/EBITDA balance sheet that management itself says is above target. 6.0% is the unlevered rate for the asset, which is what the flows are. Same rate in all three scenarios: cyclicality, Middle East exposure and the Films peak are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once). Sensitivity grid runs 4-8%.
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP (new ASBJ lease standard not yet applied at FY2026). Operating leases are already expensed inside operating profit, so no lease_cost_pct_path is charged. Finance-lease liabilities of JPY6,535m (FY2026 yuho contract-liabilities table) are treated as debt once, in equity_bridge, and excluded from the flows. Treatment (A).
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated EBITDA includes the 49% Mitsubishi Corporation share of Toyobo MC Corporation (Environmental and Functional Materials JV) and other minorities; NCI profit share was JPY3,069m of JPY14,243m consolidated profit in FY2026 (21.5%). Charged ONCE: NCI book value of JPY37,280m (2026-06-30) is deducted in equity_bridge; the flows are left consolidated. A flow-leakage alternative (~20% of NOPAT in perpetuity) would deduct more (~50-60bn PV), so the book deduction is the more generous of the two consistent treatments.
inputs.non_operating_assets_note: Dividend income (JPY405m FY2026) and interest income are outside operating profit and therefore outside the EBITDA-based flows; the matching asset, investment securities of JPY11,784m at 2026-03-31 (of which listed shares JPY5,943m at fair value, remainder unlisted/equity-method), is added in equity_bridge. Net defined-benefit position (liability 13,129 less plan asset 12,291 at 2026-06-30 = 838) deducted as debt-like. Loan guarantees for affiliates (JPY5,775m) are contingent and not deducted.
inputs.mid_cycle_note: FY2026 is treated as a Films-segment peak, not a run-rate: Films operating profit went 6.9bn -> 16.6bn (+140%) on MLCC release film and polarizer film while Life Science fell 2.0bn -> 0.1bn. FY2027 guidance (issued 2026-08-06 after a Middle East delay) is OP 23.0bn / revenue 435bn, i.e. EBITDA margin ~11.1% vs FY2026's 12.5%; Q1 FY2027 OP +28% YoY suggests the guide is conservative. Base year-1 EBITDA margin is set at 11.2% (guidance, not FY2026) and the base terminal margin at 12.3% -- between the 10-year average (10.9%) and the FY2026 print, well short of the 2030 plan's 15.2% (76.2bn / 500bn), which is the bull case.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing row: non-US cyclical operating company, owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Fresh build, no prior DCF or memory entry. Flows are unlevered: EBITDA -> D&A -> cash tax -> NOPAT + D&A - capex - working capital; interest paid (2,878) is a financing flow and is NOT in the FCF. last_fcf is FY2026 reported FCF (OCF 45,032 - capex 29,150) since SBC = 0 and interest income is not stripped (net-debt company; the dividend stream is handled by the securities bridge). Cash tax path ramps 26% -> 30.6% (Japan effective statutory) over three years: FY2026 current tax was 24.7% of pre-tax profit and ~5bn of DTAs on tax-loss carry-forwards remain; the 1,720 cash paid in FY2026 was timing against 5,661 in FY2025. Working-capital capture is NEGATIVE (-20% of the revenue change): a manufacturer with receivables + inventories well above payables consumes cash when it grows (FY2026 WC moved -6.9bn on flat revenue). Capex held at ~7% of revenue (FY2026 6.9%; FY2017-21 average ~6.5%; FY2022-25 growth wave 10.7%) with D&A at 5.9-6.0% -- the 2030 plan shifts capital toward Priority businesses, so capex stays above D&A. Terminal cap 15x FCF in base (~5x EBITDA at the terminal FCF conversion) -- a cyclical cap per the method; Gordon at 6%/1.5% would be 22.6x. House and street coincide (SBC-zero): band_position null.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Blend of equity 5yr CAGR (2.8%), FY2027 revenue guidance (+3.2%) and the 2030 plan's implied 3.5% revenue CAGR; revenue 5yr CAGR of 4.6% is inflated by the FY2022 post-COVID and price-pass-through jump
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 2.8% vs revenue 5yr 4.6% (>30% relative gap) and EPS 5yr 21.8% off the FY2021 trough (JPY47.3); EPS 3yr and FCF 3yr CAGRs are undefined because FY2023 EPS (-7.37) and FY2023 FCF (-31,360) were negative. Owner FCF has been negative in 5 of the last 10 fiscal years (FY2019, FY2022-FY2025); the 5yr FCF CAGR of 16% runs from a 7.5bn FY2021 base and should not be read as trend growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series equals reported FCF throughout (SBC = 0, interest income not stripped). Shareholders' equity is parent-only (excludes NCI, which grew from ~14bn to 38.7bn FY2023-FY2026 on the Toyobo MC JV).

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = FY2027 guidance (+3.2% to 435bn); Y2-5 at 3.0% lands FY2031 revenue ~490bn vs the plan's 500bn; fades to 2.0% (Japan nominal GDP-ish) by Y8.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 11.2% = FY2027 guided OP 23.0bn + D&A ~25.7bn over 435bn; rebuilds to 12.3% by Y6 (OP margin ~6.3%), i.e. back to FY2026's EBITDA margin but not the plan's 9% OP margin.
base.capex_rationale: 7.0% through FY2031 (plan-period investment in Priority businesses), easing to 6.5% once the portfolio shift is done; capex/D&A ~1.1x.

bull.rationale: 2030 Medium-Term Plan delivered on schedule: revenue ~500bn and EBITDA margin 15% (76.2bn) by FY2031, funded by higher plan-period capex; FY2027 guide beaten as Q1's +28% OP run-rate implies.

bear.rationale: Films peak unwinds (MLCC/polarizer film normalises), Middle East escalation keeps desalination membranes and Gulf textiles depressed, Life Science stays loss-making on Chinese diagnostics competition; EBITDA margin settles at 10.5%, below the 10-year average of 10.9% but above the FY2023-24 trough of 7%.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands near guidance (revenue 435bn, OP ~23bn) as the Films segment gives back part of its FY2026 jump and Middle East disruption weighs on membranes and Gulf textiles; thereafter revenue compounds ~3% and the EBITDA margin rebuilds to ~12.3% by FY2032 as Priority-business capital (industrial film, engineering plastics, electronics materials) rises from 27% to 50%+ of capital employed. The 2030 plan's 9% operating margin is NOT reached; ROIC stays near 5-6%, roughly the cost of capital, which is why the equity value sits at a fraction of book. Capex stays above D&A through the plan period and the cash tax rate normalises to 30.6% as loss carry-forwards are consumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: The MLCC release-film / AI-server capacitor cycle and polarizer protective film keep Films at FY2026 profitability or better, engineering plastics and VYLON adhesives grow through the Toyobo MC JV, Life Science recovers as new plants ramp, and the 2030 plan is delivered on time: revenue ~500bn and EBITDA ~76bn (15%) by FY2031 with Net Debt/EBITDA back below 4.0x. Even here the value is capped by the ~7.5% plan-period capex and a 16x FCF exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 proves to be a cyclical Films peak: MLCC and polarizer-film demand normalises, the Middle East conflict escalates (desalination membrane and traditional Arabic fabric sales, logistics costs), Chinese diagnostics competition keeps Life Science at a loss, and the 'businesses requiring improvement' (textiles, airbag fabrics, pharma CMO, packaging film) stay sub-scale. EBITDA margin settles at 10.5%, revenue stagnates for two years, and with 4.4x ND/EBITDA most of the enterprise value belongs to lenders and the Mitsubishi minority. Watch for the TV floor: the bear scenario is where the leverage shows.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: Net Debt/EBITDA 4.4x and D/E 1.22x are above management's own targets, owner FCF was negative in 5 of the last 10 years, FY2026's recovery is concentrated in one segment that management itself guides down for FY2027, and the Middle East exposure is live and, by management's own words, not fully modelled. Bull cut to 20%: the 2030 plan needs Films to hold its peak, Life Science to recover, textiles/airbags to be fixed and deleveraging to proceed simultaneously, and the completed 2025 plan missed its OP, ROE and ROIC targets. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: An unlevered owner-FCF DCF in JPY on a diversified Japanese materials manufacturer whose returns on capital have sat at or below its cost of capital for a decade (ROIC 3.8% FY2026, P/B persistently <1.0x) and whose balance sheet carries 4.4x ND/EBITDA plus a large JV minority. The flows start from FY2027 guidance rather than the FY2026 Films peak, risk is charged once in the scenarios and weights, and NCI, finance leases and the securities portfolio each enter the bridge exactly once. Because interest-bearing debt and the Mitsubishi minority together exceed JPY260bn against an enterprise value in the 250-350bn range, the equity is a thin residual and per-share value is extremely sensitive to the terminal margin and exit multiple: the stock trades as a P/E and P/B instrument on recovery earnings, not as an FCF compounder.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal EBITDA margin: each 1pp of terminal margin is worth roughly JPY400-500/share because equity is a thin residual over 260bn of debt-like claims
Capex intensity: the 2030 plan's shift of capital toward Priority businesses may hold capex at the FY2022-25 pace (~10% of revenue) rather than 7%, which would erase base-case FCF
Films-segment cyclicality (MLCC release film, polarizer protective film) -- FY2026 OP +140% in that segment is the single source of the FY2026 recovery
Middle East conflict exposure (desalination membranes, Gulf textiles) that management explicitly excluded from its plan assumptions
Rising JPY interest rates on ~255bn of borrowings, including the 2024 subordinated instrument; interest paid already rose 1,330 -> 2,878 in two years
NCI valued at book (37.3bn); the Toyobo MC JV's economic value to Mitsubishi could be higher, which would reduce the parent's share further
Discount rate: at a mechanical levered WACC (~4.5%) the value would be much higher; at the house 9% JPY keiretsu rate the equity is worthless -- the 6% unlevered rate is a judgment

valuation_notes.equity_is_a_thin_residual: Debt-like claims (net debt 226.0bn + NCI 37.3bn + finance leases 6.5bn + net pension 0.8bn - securities 11.8bn = 258.9bn) sit against a base enterprise value of 261.9bn, so the base equity is ~3bn (JPY34/share) and every 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin or 1x of exit multiple moves the per-share value by hundreds of yen. Current market EV including NCI is ~394bn (market cap 134.5bn + 258.9bn), i.e. ~7.5x FY2026 EBITDA and ~8.1x FY2027 guided EBITDA.
valuation_notes.bear_scenario_negative: The bear intrinsic value of JPY-1,311 means bear-case enterprise value (143.2bn) falls 115.7bn short of the debt-like claims; under limited liability the equity in that path is worth zero, not a negative amount. The engine weights linearly, giving weighted_iv JPY-10.7. Flooring the bear at zero (the option-value reading) gives 0.30x0 + 0.50x34.16 + 0.20x1,827.8 = JPY383/share. Both are far below the JPY1,524 price; neither is a buy signal.
valuation_notes.terminal_cap_binds_in_all_scenarios: The cyclical FCF cap (15x base / 16x bull / 13x bear) binds everywhere; Gordon at 6% WACC would be 22.6x base. Because D&A (~6% of revenue) and capex (~6.5-7%) are large relative to EBITDA, FCF converts at only ~28% of EBITDA, so the FCF cap implies a terminal EV/EBITDA of 4.2x base / 5.7x bull / 2.9x bear against ~7.5x today -- the model assumes a de-rating from the current multiple. Memo, uncapped Gordon terminal (NOT the house basis): base EV 342.1bn -> equity 83.2bn -> JPY942/share; bull JPY3,669; bear JPY-805 (zero floored); weighted JPY963 linear or JPY1,205 with the bear floored. The gap between the house JPY34 and the uncapped JPY942 is the price of assuming the market keeps paying ~6.4x EBITDA for a business earning its cost of capital at best.
valuation_notes.what_the_price_implies: At JPY1,524 the market is paying roughly the bull case (JPY1,828 house, i.e. the 2030 plan delivered: 15% EBITDA margin, 500bn revenue by FY2031) discounted ~17%, or the base case on an uncapped ~6.4x EBITDA exit plus a further ~60% premium. It is pricing the stock as a P/E (12x FY2026, 19x FY2027 guided EPS) and P/B (0.63x) recovery instrument, not on owner FCF.
valuation_notes.sanity_check_expectation: The multiples check is expected to pass: the model is below the market on every multiple, so none of the Step 8c.5 overvaluation fixes (mid-cycle FCF, WACC premium, growth cap, exit-multiple cap) apply. The mid-cycling has already been done by starting from FY2027 guidance rather than the FY2026 Films peak.
